newsitem.title: CHINA: IBM in $42.5 mln China joint venture.
newsitem.headline: IBM in $42.5 mln China joint venture.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp (IBM) said on Wednesday it was setting up a $42.5 million plant in southern China with two Chinese companies to make parts for hard disk drives.

IBM would have an 80 percent stake in Shenzhen Hailiang Storage Products Co Ltd, while Shenzhen Kaifa Technology Ltd and China Great Wall Computer Shenzhen Co would hold 10 percent each, a company statement said.

Based in Shenzhen in Guangdong province, the new company would have an annual production capacity of about 30 million magneto-resistive head gimbal assemblies, to be used in IBM hard disk drive assembly plants worldwide, it said.

"This is part of our vision to be a major player in the IT (information technology) industry by facilitating the development and transfer of advanced technology in China," it quoted Henry Chow, chairman of IBM China Co Ltd, as saying.

Shenzhen Hailiang would be IBM's biggest joint venture in China and its second project with the two Chinese firms, the statement said. Construction of the plant had already begun and production would start in the next few weeks, it said without giving further details.
